The use of the variable u in the Substitution Rule is traditional (sometimes it is referred to as u-substitution), but any letter can be used, such as y, t, u and so forth. The rule pro- vides a method for evaluating an integral of the form 1ƒ(g(x))g′(x) dx given that the condi- tions of Theorem 6 are satisfied. The primary challenge is deciding what expression involv- ing x you want to substitute for in the integrand. Our examples to follow give helpful ideas.
The Substitution Method to evaluate 1ƒ(g(x))g′(x) dx 1. Substitute u = g(x) and du = (du/dx) dx = g′(x) dx to obtain 1ƒ(u) du. 2. Integrate with respect to u. 3. Replace u by g(x).
